capabilities: Search OpenAlex weekly for each user-defined feed and rank papers into priority, strong and possible tiers
Write a weekly reading-inbox note with a filterable table, status chips, tick boxes and dismissals
Sync ticked papers into Zotero collections with feed tags, skipping papers already in the library
Report search effectiveness, topic overlap and term suggestions from a local history ledger
Build literature reviews with cost-capped OpenAlex lookups, citation-gap analysis, network graphs and copy-paste LLM prompts
extras: Not yet in the Obsidian community plugin store; the README says everything beyond the current phase describes what it is being built to do. OpenAlex requests cost paid credits with free daily allowance and per-review spending limits, and costs are stated throughout.
problem: Obsidian has no way to discover new academic papers on chosen topics and triage them into a reading queue without manual searches and manual Zotero entry.

relations.evidence: From there your usual Zotero → ZotLit → Obsidian reading workflow takes over.
Lab Kit is a separate plugin for a chemistry lab notebook. Literature Feed works with it through note conventions only
The Zotero add-on Better Find Full Text (its README lists Zotero 7.0, 8.x, 9.x and 10.x).
It is a TypeScript port of the check_refs.py script, so nothing needs installing.

summary: Academic literature discovery that searches OpenAlex weekly into a reading-inbox note and syncs ticked papers to your Zotero library.
